messages:
incident-bot: SEV2 paging: multiple model-warmup failures in region us-west-2 impacting /v1/chat. Symptoms: model deserialization errors, cuda OOM during load, kernel JIT timeouts. Auto-escalation threshold crossed: warmup failure rate > 15% for 7m.
Priya Rao: I'm awake, jumping in. seeing a cluster of errors tied to model 'redwood-7b-quant-v2' warmup. Logs show repeated 'read: unexpected EOF' while streaming weights and then 'cudaMalloc returned resource exhausted'.
Marcus (oncall): taking ownership. Which nodes are affected? Any under maintenance?
Liam Eng: gpunode-12 and gpunode-13 showing OOMKills on runtime pods. kubectl events: "OOMKilled process blrtd"; docker logs show long compile phase: "jit: kernel compile exceeded 45s". Also artifact-service returned 503s around 17:02 UTC which may have led to partial artifact reads.
artifact-bot: Artifact fetch event: model redwood-7b-quant-v2 fetch failed 3x from artifact-store-2 (503 ServiceUnavailable) at 2026-06-11T17:02:12Z.
Nia SRE: Heatmap: warmup concurrency was at 8 for that model due to recent autoscale. Combined with compile bursts, memory pressure peaked. Suggest immediate mitigation: throttle warmup and avoid simultaneous compile on same node.
Marcus (oncall): mitigation action plan (short): 1) pause auto-warmup for redwood-7b-quant-v2 in us-west-2 2) set warmup concurrency=2 3) flip routing to variant-medium for standard tier 4) cordon gpunode-12 and migrate pods. Applying now.
Priya Rao: applying config: `service.flags.warmup_enabled=false` for model:redwood-7b-quant-v2 (us-west-2). Also pushing `warmup.concurrency=2`.
Simon Platform: also recommending to disable jit-kernel-cache warmup step (`--warmup-jit=false`) — prepopulating JIT increases memory spikes. Going to apply for the affected model.
Liam Eng: applied `--warmup-jit=false` and reduced prefetch buffers: `runtime.prefetch=0`. Logs afterwards show fewer compile attempts.
aws-bot: ASG update: scaling activity suppressed for gpunodepool-west for 10m per request from ops.
Marcus (oncall): how's customer impact? Olga, any alerts from CS?
Olga PS: CS report: hosted API saw p95 latency climb from 140ms to 2.1s during peak; approx 1.2% of requests returned 500s for ~10 minutes. Two enterprise customers on dedicated had intermittent failures (5-10 requests each). Sending an update to affected customers now.
Marcus (oncall): good. Dave (not present) had recommended earlier to stagger warmups; Simon, can we get a short-term rate limiter in front of warmup queue?
Simon Platform: implementing token-bucket limiter (burst=2, rate=1/s) for warmup scheduler. Will gate at the scheduler layer; rolling out in 60s.
Priya Rao: monitoring: warmup failure rate dropping from 18% -> 4% after changes. GPU free memory on gpunode-13 increased by ~9GB.
Liam Eng: note from logs: several 'EOF while reading chunk' entries timestamped just before OOMs. artifact-bot indicates the artifact store had transient 503s; possible corrupt partial reads causing deserialization EOF. Filing ticket ART-592.
artifact-bot: Ticket ART-592 created: investigate artifact-store 503s around 2026-06-11T17:02Z.
Marcus (oncall): node ops: cordon gpunode-12; drain in progress. migrating pods to gpunode-15 with extra headroom.
Nia SRE: autoscaler tweak: set maxPodsPerNode to 18 for gpunodepool-west to avoid dense packing; disabling binpack to spread warmups.
Olga PS: customer comms drafted: "We've applied temporary routing to reduce cold-start failures and are investigating root cause (artifact fetch retries + compile spikes). We'll follow up with timeline and remediation plan." Sending now.
Simon Platform: longer-term proposals: 1) pre-validate artifact hashes before warmup to detect incomplete downloads 2) limit parallel JIT compilations per node 3) warmup queue rate-limiter and priority for enterprise customers. Filing RFC.
Marcus (oncall): is there any risk of repeat while artifact store ticket pending?
Priya Rao: the biggest risk is another artifact outage during heavy churn; mitigations in place reduce concurrency and JITs so even if artifact is flaky, OOM should be much less likely.
incident-bot: Automation log: applied warmup concurrency change for 3 services; disabled warmup-JIT for redwood-7b-quant-v2 in us-west-2; token-bucket warmup limiter deployed.
Priya Rao: realtime metrics: warmup error rate now at 2.7%, p95 latency back down to 180ms. No new OOMKills reported in last 6m.
Olga PS: customers notified; one customer asked for dedicated warmup window — ops offered to schedule. They accepted; CS coordinating.
Marcus (oncall): assigning postmortem owners: Priya Rao (lead), Simon Platform (mitigation design), Nia SRE (ops follow-up), Olga PS (customer comms). Draft due in 36h.
Liam Eng: follow-up: increase artifact fetch retries with exponential backoff in client (3 retries -> 6 retries), and validate partial read error handling to avoid deserializing partial blobs. I'll open a PR.
artifact-bot: ART-592 updated with link to artifact fetch logs and shard metrics.
incident-bot: Incident mitigated; severity reduced to SEV2 (stable). Oncall handoff in 25m.
Marcus (oncall): staying on until handoff. If warmup failures creep above 10% again, escalate to SEV1. Thanks all. :thumbsup:
Priya Rao: adding timeline and logs to the postmortem doc. Including repro steps and a small script to reproduce warmup EOF when artifact-store returns partial payload.
incident-bot: Auto-close active paging at 3955554380 (no active alerts)."
